clarity.name: Clarity
clarity.meaning: People are not working to the same picture of "good". The standard, the target or the reason behind it is not shared.
moves: Write the standard in one sentence people can repeat.
Show what good looks like with a real example, not a slide.
Explain why the number matters to the next person in the process.
clarity.question: Ask three people: what does "done right" look like here?

skill.name: Skill
skill.meaning: The process can work, but not everyone can run it reliably yet. Experience is carrying the result.
moves: Pair newer people with a strong performer for a few shifts.
Turn the critical steps into a one-page checklist.
Check understanding by watching the work, not by asking "is it clear?"
skill.question: Where exactly does it go wrong the first time someone does this alone?

capacity.name: Capacity
capacity.meaning: The work does not fit into the time or people available. Steps are dropped under pressure.
moves: Put the KPI next to volume and staffing by hour or by day.
Protect the critical steps at peak time and drop the non-essential ones first.
Move work away from the peak wherever you can.
capacity.question: What do people skip when it gets busy?

design.name: Process design
design.meaning: The process itself produces the error. Different people get the same result because the system leads them there.
moves: Walk the process end to end and time each step.
Make the right way the easy way: layout, tools, defaults.
Remove steps that only exist because of old problems.
design.question: What makes the wrong way faster than the right way?

ownership.name: Ownership
ownership.meaning: The work falls between people, shifts or teams. Everyone does their part, and the gap belongs to nobody.
moves: Name one owner for each handoff.
Agree what "handed over" means: what, in which state, by when.
Review misses at the handoff, not only at the end of the line.
ownership.question: At which moment does this become nobody's job?

statements.text: If you ask different people what the standard is, you get different answers.
The number gets worse at peak times, on busy days or with fewer people on shift.
The same error keeps coming back, even when different people do the work.
The problem is concentrated among newer or less experienced people.
Problems appear at handoffs between shifts, teams or systems.
The target changed recently, or the reason behind it was never explained.
Tools, layout or systems make the right way slower than the wrong way.
People skip steps because there is not enough time to do them all.
When something goes wrong, it is unclear who should have caught it.
Results improve clearly when an experienced person is on the same shift.
